questions.question: Describe the ANC's early methods and explain why the Youth League called for change.
questions.expected_answer: SANNC founded 8 January 1912 (renamed ANC 1923) by educated leaders (Dube, Seme, Plaatje); moderate methods: petitions, letters, deputations (Britain 1914, 1919), 1919 anti-pass campaign; ICU (Kadalie). Laws became harsher (Urban Areas Act 1923, Cape vote removed 1936, Land Act 1936). Youth League 1944: Lembede (African nationalism), Mda, Sisulu, Tambo, Mandela; wanted self-reliance, mass movement and militant methods; 1948 NP victory increased urgency.

questions.question: Explain the Programme of Action of 1949 and the events of 1950.
questions.expected_answer: Adopted December 1949 Bloemfontein: national freedom, rejection of apartheid, direct representation; mass non-violent action: boycotts (advisory councils, NRC), strikes, civil disobedience, non-cooperation; national unity. Moroka replaced Xuma; Sisulu secretary-general. 1 May 1950 May Day strike (CP, TIC, Transvaal ANC): 18 killed by police. 26 June 1950 National Day of Protest and Mourning with SAIC; 26 June later used for Defiance Campaign (1952) and Freedom Charter (1955). Closer alliance between ANC, Indian congresses, others; Africanist tensions (PAC 1959).

questions.question: Explain the Suppression of Communism Act and how it was used to repress opposition.
questions.expected_answer: CPSA formed 1921, non-racial, majority rule, unions; Cold War anti-communism and fear of black organisation. 1950 Act declared CP unlawful; CP dissolved itself June 1950, re-formed underground as SACP 1953 (banned until 1990). Very broad definition (any change by disorder or hostility between races) = "statutory communism". Minister could ban people without trial: no gatherings, restricted areas, resign from organisations, not quoted; later house arrest; used against ANC leaders, unionists, journalists, church members.
